content.figure: Figure 8: Selection of invasive strategy and reperfusion therapy in patients presenting with NSTE-ACS
content.summary: Guidance for risk stratification and selection of invasive/reperfusion strategy in patients with non–ST-elevation acute coronary syndrome (NSTE-ACS). Patients are triaged by risk (very high, high, non-high) to determine timing of invasive angiography and reperfusion.
content.risk_stratification_overview: Determine risk at first medical contact (FMC) and transfer appropriately (non-PCI centre, ambulance, or PCI centre). Very-high-risk patients require immediate transfer and invasive strategy. High-risk patients should undergo early (<24 h) or inpatient invasive strategy. Non-high-risk patients may undergo selective invasive or inpatient invasive strategy based on clinical course.
very_high_risk_features: Recurrent or ongoing chest pain refractory to medical treatment
Acute heart failure presumed secondary to ongoing myocardial ischemia
Life-threatening arrhythmias or cardiac arrest after presentation
Recurrent dynamic ECG changes suggestive of ischemia
high_risk_features: Confirmed diagnosis of NSTEMI based on ESC algorithms

management_recommendations.very_high_risk: Immediate invasive strategy and immediate transfer to PCI centre (Class I).
management_recommendations.high_risk: Early (<24 h) invasive angiography and inpatient invasive strategy (Class I / Class IIa depending on specific features).
management_recommendations.non_high_risk: Selective invasive strategy or inpatient invasive strategy if required; invasive strategy during admission for patients with high index of suspicion for unstable angina.

abbreviations_and_definitions.GRACE: Global Registry of Acute Coronary Events

content.notes: Patients meeting any single very-high-risk NSTE-ACS criterion should undergo an immediate invasive strategy. Patients with high-risk criteria (e.g., confirmed NSTEMI by hs-cTn-based ESC algorithm, GRACE >140, dynamic ECG changes) should be considered for early invasive angiography within 24 hours.
